expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant has only 'cancelReason' and 'isVoluntary'; no retry/grace/trial fields present

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: switch statement shown without default case or assertNever call; relies on implicit type-checker behavior without explicit implementation

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: id: Brand<string, "SubscriptionId">; customerId: Brand<string, "CustomerId">; export type Instant = Brand<string, ...>; export type RetryCount = Brand<number, ...>

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "A `trialing` subscription without a trial-end date. A canceled subscription carrying retry/grace-period fields. An active subscription accidentally treated as if it had a cancellation reason. A status typo."

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "Use a discriminated union—each status carries exactly the fields that are valid for it"
